summary: Verified 7.0/10, NOT ON PAR (below 7.5; no blocker open). art/out/fighters/vashil is unchanged since 874f3f6d1 (git diff empty, no working-tree changes), so the reviewer's measurements still describe the build. The cowl fix holds: R at 3 cm is 14.3 cm and the width 5 cm under the top is 20.2 cm against ruling 7's 10 cm (closing_vashil_crown.txt; I recomputed it as (8.75^2+3^2)/6). In the real RIFT frame the silhouette reads well. VAS2-M1 (cards) is confirmed: splash.png is a static back-three-quarter stand, a posterized cut-out in warm light on a cool plate. VAS2-M2 (attack1/attack2/cast_a3 timing) is confirmed from the perframe report: Ring Out moves the rod 1.756 m in one 30 Hz key at about 1.33x, and attack2 stutters with near-zero keys at f3 and f6. VAS2-M3 (no signature hue) is downgraded to minor. In the reviewer's own chroma table Vashil's C* p50 is 5.3, the 4th highest of 16 fighters (Marund and Tunlan 1.9, Sukri 2.2). Only on p90 is he low, and five fighters share that pale band, so it is a roster art-direction call, not a Vashil defect. Even so, the cards and the attack timing keep him at 7.0. No missed sensitivity problem: the halo's top finial is a hard part (ruling 7 exempts finials) and reads as a spire on the ring, not a hood. The Chalkline face grille stays minor.

gapStatus.evidence: _harness/_reports/closing_vashil_crown.txt: width 0.175 / depth 0.191 at 3 cm, so R = 14.3 cm, and width 0.202 at 5 cm on all three skins (the profiles are identical); ruling 7 needs 10 cm. GLBs are unchanged since the measurement (git diff 874f3f6d1..HEAD empty).
closing_vashil_range.txt: recall hand.L 0.597 m, halo 0.141 m (was 0.004 m).
closing_vashil_perframe.txt: the largest rod step in cast_a1 is 0.317 m and in cast_ult 0.308 m per 30 Hz key (fixed). attack1 0.877, attack2 1.073 and cast_a3 1.756 m remain (VAS2-M2).
The three skins now differ in pose and plate. The cards are still posterized cut-out stands (splash.png viewed; VAS2-M1).
build_report accentPct 0.43 / 0.38 / 0.33 (base / chalkline / first_bell); beads in closing_vashil_portraits.png.
No close rod render newer than _fit/compare_rod.png (Oct 27); nothing is visible at the game camera.

findings.title: Portraits and splashes are posterized model renders pasted on painted plates, with stiff poses and mismatched light
findings.what: The base splash (viewed full size) is a static stand, turned three-quarter away. The raised wrist covers the cowl side. A warm peach figure with a hard cut-out edge and smeared brush planes sits on a cool blue dusk plate, and the figure casts no light or shadow into the scene. All three portrait crops cut through the bell ring.
findings.gauge: A LoL splash is fully painted in its scene: one dynamic key moment, a focal face or prop lit by the scene's own light, and painted edges with atmospheric depth.
findings.fix: As the reviewer proposes: one signature VALE action moment per skin (for example a Morning Toll strike on bell-stone, or chalk sound-lines drawn by the rod tip), relit with the plate's key and fill before stylizing, a hand paint-over at 2x, and portraits recomposed around the visor and the two front bells.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed visually. This is the biggest gap against the gauge.

findings.title: Basic attacks and Ring Out snap through the swing in one key, freeze after it, and stutter in the wind-up
findings.what: Ring Out (cast_a3) moves the rod head 1.756 m at f8. With castTime 0.2 s and impact at f8 (0.267 s) it plays at 1.33x, about 1.17 m per 60 Hz display frame, against the 0.3 m bar that Peal and Toll now meet. attack2 moves the rod 1.073 m at f8 (attack windup 0.24 s, so about 1.1x), then nearly freezes over f9-f11 (0.043 / 0.001 / 0.053 m). Its wind-up hitches at f3 (0.067 m) and f6 (0.060 m) between steps of 0.242 and 0.545 m.
findings.gauge: LoL autos and sweeps spread the strike over 2-3 frames, often with a smear, after an evenly eased anticipation.
findings.fix: Re-time with an arc pass. Remove the near-zero wind-up keys. Spread the strike over 2-3 keys. Keep a short impact hold, but with 2-4 cm of body drift and the bells still swinging. Gate the clips at 0.3 m per display frame with art/tools/clip_steps.py.
findings.verifierNote: Partly refuted on one point: a brief hold on the hit is a legitimate impact hold, not a defect in itself. The one-key snap on Ring Out and the wind-up stutter are real, and the same metric made VAS-M2 a major before.

findings.title: Body hue is pale tan; identity leans on the halo shape
findings.what: The figure reads as a pale tan, grey and slate robe with almost no team tint (accent 0.43 %).
findings.evidence: _harness/_reports/closing_vashil_roster_chroma.txt: Vashil C* p50 5.3 (4th highest of 16; Marund and Tunlan 1.9, Sukri 2.2, Hesmi 2.4) and p90 7.0 (tied 5th lowest with Ervet; Marund 6.0, Ardit 6.3, Lisvel 6.5)
findings.gauge: LoL reads champions silhouette first and colour second. A signature hue mass helps in teamfights, but a strong unique silhouette such as the bell ring carries identity at the gameplay camera.
findings.fix: Optional: a muted dawn-lilac-grey VALE signature on the stole and sash (saturation 25-35 %, outside the reserved bands), checked with lineup_qa and card_qa.
findings.verifierNote: Downgraded from major. The 'among the lowest' claim holds only on p90; on median chroma he is above most of the roster. The pale band is a roster-wide art direction shared by five fighters, and his silhouette is unique and reads in the real match frame (closing_vashil_match_f0_x4.png).

findings.title: Chalkline face plate: a dark recess around a pale relief reads as a grille or teeth at 2x
findings.what: At 2x the swirl relief in the ink-dark box under the visor reads as teeth. At portrait size it reads as a helmet breathing grille, not horror.
findings.gauge: A visored face keeps one clear focal read at chip size.
findings.fix: Lift the recess to L* 40-45 and redraw the relief as horizontal chalk sound-lines.
findings.verifierNote: Checked for the blocker class and it is not one: at use size it reads as a knight-style grille under a glass visor, not a horror face. Worth fixing because it is the closest the roster comes.

findings.title: Stunned is a spinning halo on a still body
findings.what: Hips 0.000 m and chest 0.017 m; only the halo and head move.
findings.gauge: LoL stun loops show a whole-body daze.
findings.fix: Soften the knees and let the rod drift and the head lag.

findings.title: Upright, low-bob run with a rigid floor-length robe
findings.what: Hips and chest move about 3 cm in the run; only the sleeves have secondary bones.
findings.gauge: Robed casters lean into the run and the hem trails the stride.
findings.fix: Add a forward lean and spring chains on the hem and stole.

findings.title: Death ends under a level, floating halo
findings.what: The bell ring stays level above the slumped body.
findings.gauge: The signature prop resolves in the death pose.
findings.fix: Tip and drop the ring and dim the bells.
